messages:
Dana (FinOps): Heads up — OrbisAI invoice INV-2026-014 shows a `surge_charge` line for 2026-02-28 ~ 68 GPU-hours (~$4,120). Vendor labeled it 'elastic_surge'. Anyone seen this pattern? :eyes:
Sam (Acct Mgr): Noted. I'm pinging the vendor for raw meter logs. Do we know if Orbis was on any burst policy or did they exceed their reserved commit?
billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-014 generated for customer: OrbisAI. reserved_commit_hours=1600, billed_usage_hours=1668, surge_hours=68, surge_amount=$4,120.
Vera (Customer Success): Orbis says they ran a large eval and had a planned failover at ~22:00 UTC; they expected failover to use reserved pool but reported it went to a different pool (eu-west1-ephemeral). They asked for reversal.
Omar (SRE): Checked autoscaler events quickly: `kubectl logs deployment/orbis-eval-autoscaler --since=48h | grep "scale"` shows a spike 2026-02-28T21:47Z scale 8 -> 24 due to job `orbis-offline-eval`. Nodes in eu-west1 were labeled `node-pool: ephemeral`; looks like the job picked wrong nodeSelector.
Omar (SRE): TL;DR: infra mis-tag meant customer workload landed outside dedicated reserved pool, vendor charged as surge.
Dana (FinOps): If that's the case, policy usually charges customer for misconfiguration, but first-time mistakes sometimes get goodwill. What options do we have?
Eli (Legal): Policy note: We can make an administrative one-time credit if vendor confirms meter mapping and if customer agrees to remedial steps. Full reversal is not standard unless vendor billing error.
Sam (Acct Mgr): Propose: (1) request vendor audit/reclassification of those 68 hours (2) offer Orbis a one-time goodwill credit up to 50% of surge ($2,060) if they sign a 6-month commit addendum and tag their workloads correctly.
Vera (Customer Success): Orbis is pushing for full reversal — they're midmarket and worried about churn. If we offer partial credit + short-term commit, we might retain them. They want SLA assurance on failover routing.
Dana (FinOps): I'm willing to approve up to $2,500 goodwill credit contingent on: vendor audit request, customer signs commit addendum, and engineering runs a quick runbook to prevent future mis-tagging. Sam, can you draft terms?
Sam (Acct Mgr): Will do. I will: (a) open vendor reclassification request, (b) send draft addendum to Orbis, (c) create internal ticket for SRE to add runbook and tagging check.
billing-bot: Created vendor ticket VND-4521 for meter audit and reclassification request. Created internal ticket FIN-3378 for credit approval workflow.
Omar (SRE): I'll add a preflight check to the deploy pipeline to ensure `nodeSelector: dedicated-pool` present for `orbis-*` jobs and document the failover expectations in runbook RB-122.
Eli (Legal): Once Sam has the addendum signed we'll route the credit through FIN-3378 and confirm compliance.
Sam (Acct Mgr): I'll update here after vendor responds and after Orbis signs. Planning to propose $2,060 credit, vendor permitting reclassification.
Vera (Customer Success): I'll coordinate with Orbis on the addendum and get their operations lead on a quick call with Omar.
Dana (FinOps): Approved up to $2.5k goodwill as discussed. If vendor finds a billing error, we'll reverse fully. Otherwise proceed with the credit path. :thumbsup:
Sam (Acct Mgr): Thanks. Marking this thread in my queue. Will post vendor response and signed addendum.
billing-bot: FIN-3378 updated: status=awaiting_vendor_response.
Dana (FinOps): Closing note: follow-up required — Sam to confirm vendor outcome by EOD+3.
Sam (Acct Mgr): Roger. I'll update thread.
